{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-la-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e70bab0886d3a40cb670b5a1aeb30e1f4118be72b9d243a035626e87acd8984d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-la-class-std:lineage:64","source_registry_sha256":"8fb2294cb50570a3a0fabb25acba3418dba999eb7dd305cc58b73fdf38975613","source_liveness_sha256":"1105a92b5841d065519de4b7fbea05111880de6d2bb8804066a972d19c63b5a0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges","heading":"Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"# Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol or certain drugs is a crime. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Alcohol is a depressant rather than a stimulant. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Alcohol can slow reflexes, impair judgment, reduce alertness and affect vision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Lowered inhibition after drinking can create a misleading feeling of stimulation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
The amount of alcohol reaching the blood matters rather than whether the beverage is beer, wine or spirits. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Food intake and drinking rate can affect how rapidly alcohol is absorbed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
Coffee, exercise and cold showers do not make an impaired person sober. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Eliminating alcohol takes time rather than a quick sobering trick. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
Alcohol can impair judging speed, distance and angles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
Drinking can reduce caution and encourage unsafe risks or traffic violations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
Alcohol-impaired concentration can lead a driver to omit signals, lights or other driving tasks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
Alcohol can slow the response needed for a stop or turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
An impaired person may misjudge the degree of personal impairment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
Alcohol can cause drowsiness and blurred vision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A02
Do not let a person known to have been drinking operate the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A02
Blood alcohol concentration describes the amount of alcohol in a measured volume of blood. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A02
A breath test can be used to estimate alcohol concentration without taking a blood sample. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
For noncommercial drivers age twenty-one or older, the guide states a BAC threshold of 0.08 percent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
For drivers younger than twenty-one, the guide states a BAC threshold of 0.02 percent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A03
Even one alcoholic drink can affect the ability to operate a vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A03
Weaving, erratic speed, abrupt stopping or unusually slow driving may indicate impairment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A03
The guide describes Louisiana restrictions on both consuming alcohol and possessing an open alcoholic-beverage container in a vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A03
A DWI conviction can result in criminal penalties and loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]
